title: Swedish Institute (SI) Scholarships & University Admissions Sweden Ranking Strategy

runs.t: Sweden’s Swedish Institute (SI) Scholarship for Global Professionals is a competitive funding opportunity for international professionals who want to pursue an eligible master’s programme in Sweden and use the experience to contribute to sustainable development in their home country or region. For Indian applicants, the strategy has two connected parts: secure a strong, eligible university application through University Admissions, then submit a separate SI scholarship application that meets the scholarship’s country, work-experience, leadership and document requirements.

The order in which you rank programmes matters. Sweden’s central admissions system considers your highest-ranked choice first; if you receive an offer for a higher-ranked master’s programme, the lower-ranked choices are removed from consideration.

For Autumn 2027, the international first admissions round opens on 16 October 2026 and closes on 15 January 2027. Applicants can rank up to four master’s programmes. The SI scholarship application window is separate and is scheduled for 8–24 February 2027. SI funding is limited to eligible programmes and eligible applicants; check the official 2027/28 country list, programme list and application templates before proceeding. Do not treat the scholarship as an automatic tuition waiver for every Swedish master’s degree.

sections.title: What does the SI Scholarship for Global Professionals cover?

runs.t: The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is designed to support professionals with leadership potential and a clear plan to contribute to sustainable development in their home country or region. The 2027/28 call information available at the research cut-off describes the following funding components. Applicants must verify the final official call terms before applying.

rows.t: Tuition fee
SI pays the tuition fee directly to the Swedish university for the awarded programme and study period.
Only the awarded eligible programme is covered; programme changes and extensions are not allowed.
Living allowance
SEK 12,000 per month.
Compare this with your own city and accommodation budget; it is a fixed scholarship allowance, not a promise that every lifestyle cost is covered.
Travel grant
One-time SEK 15,000 for eligible scholars.
Check exclusions, including applicants already living in Sweden and any country-specific exceptions.
Professional network
Membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals and later the Sweden Alumni Network.
Network participation is a programme benefit, not a job-placement guarantee.
Not covered / separate
University Admissions application fee, insurance and family-member costs are not included in the described scholarship package.
Budget separately and confirm insurance arrangements with the university.

runs.t: Eligibility is country-specific and can change between scholarship cycles. Before preparing documents, confirm that India appears in the official SI Scholarship for Global Professionals eligible-country list for the 2027/28 call. Do not rely on a previous year’s country list or a third-party scholarship directory.

The current call information also sets professional experience and leadership requirements for applicants from most eligible countries. The 2027/28 call information available at the research cut-off states that applicants from the main country group must document at least 3,000 hours of work experience before February 2027, from no more than three employers. It also requires leadership experience. Applicants should read the official country-specific exception list carefully; some countries have different work-hour rules.

sections.title: Work experience and leadership: prepare evidence, not just a CV

runs.t: The scholarship is aimed at professionals. A CV that lists job titles without evidence may not be enough. Applicants should document responsibilities, employment dates, hours and leadership impact using the SI templates for the relevant year.

rows.t: Work experience
Employer certificates and other proof requested by SI, showing roles and dates.
Calculate the qualifying hours carefully. Use only the number of employers allowed by the call.
Leadership
Evidence of leadership through employment, entrepreneurship or civil-society engagement, as permitted by the call.
Show what you led, who benefited, what changed and your own responsibility.
References
Two reference letters in the current SI format, where required by the call.
Choose referees who can give specific examples of professional performance and leadership.
Motivation
A clear explanation of why the programme matters and how it supports development in your home country or region.
Connect the proposed study to a credible post-study contribution plan, not only personal career advancement.

runs.t: Do not manufacture or inflate hours, titles or leadership roles. SI can disqualify applications that do not follow the required templates or evidence instructions.

sections.title: University Admissions Sweden: how the ranking system works

runs.t: For master’s applicants, University Admissions provides one application portal for programmes offered by Swedish universities. Applicants can select up to four master’s programmes and rank them in genuine order of preference.

head.t: What it means for an applicant

rows.t: Rank the programme you most want first
Your first choice is assessed first in the selection process.
Only one master’s offer
You can be admitted to only one master’s programme in the round.
Lower-ranked options can be deleted
If you receive an offer for a higher-ranked programme, the programmes below it are removed and are not considered.
Ranking locks at the deadline
For Autumn 2027, the last day to apply and rank is 15 January 2027.
Eligibility is not admission
Meeting entry requirements does not guarantee an offer; selection depends on available places and programme-specific merit criteria.

runs.t: Do not rank programmes simply by university reputation or global ranking. Start with academic fit and your intended career direction. A well-ranked programme that does not match your previous coursework may be a weaker choice than a less famous programme with a stronger academic fit.
Define the target role or research area you want to pursue after graduation.
Identify the academic prerequisites for each programme, including required credits in mathematics, computing, engineering, economics or other subject areas.
Check the exact degree title, curriculum, electives, thesis structure, internship or industry links and teaching language.
Compare the selection criteria and required supporting documents on the programme page.
Assess the total tuition fee and city-level living costs, not just the university’s name.
Rank your true first preference first, then the next most preferred options. Do not use a “safe” programme as the first choice if you would not accept it over the others.
Check whether each programme is on the current SI eligible-programme list if you intend to apply for the SI scholarship.

sections.title: KTH master’s programmes: an example of programme-level scrutiny

runs.t: KTH Royal Institute of Technology offers a broad range of master’s programmes across engineering, computer science, architecture, industrial management and related areas. Its admissions guidance states that applicants generally need a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Swedish bachelor’s degree, English proficiency equivalent to Swedish upper-secondary English 6, and programme-specific prerequisites. The university’s 2026 admissions information reports an average acceptance rate of 31% for its master’s programmes, but this is not a predictive acceptance rate for an individual course or applicant.

KTH’s published fee information states that the full tuition fee for most two-year programmes with both years at KTH is SEK 385,000, while fees vary by programme. The application fee through University Admissions is SEK 900 for applicants who are required to pay. Always check the specific programme page and intake-year fee.

For Indian applicants, a programme shortlist should test whether the undergraduate degree contains the subject credits KTH requires. For example, a computer science master’s may require a defined set of mathematics and computing credits; a general engineering degree does not automatically meet every programme’s prerequisites.

sections.title: Autumn 2027 timeline: university application and SI scholarship are separate

rows.t: 16 October 2026
University Admissions first round opens.
Create account, research programmes and prepare documents.
15 January 2027
Application deadline and last day to rank.
Submit up to four master’s choices in priority order.
1 February 2027
Application fee and supporting-document deadline.
Pay fee if required and ensure all documents are uploaded.
8–24 February 2027
SI scholarship application window (published call schedule).
Submit one scholarship application using the correct 2027/28 templates.
1 April 2027
Master’s admissions results.
Check whether admitted or conditionally admitted to an eligible programme.
22 April 2027
SI scholarship announcement (published call schedule).
Check the official SI announcement and respond to any offer by its stated deadline.

runs.t: Dates are subject to official updates. Applicants must complete both processes: a University Admissions application and a separate SI scholarship application. Missing the university application or documentation deadline can make a candidate ineligible for the scholarship process.
Assuming every Indian applicant is automatically eligible without checking the 2027/28 country list.
Applying for a programme that is not included in the current SI eligible-programme list.
Confusing the university application with the SI scholarship application.
Ranking a programme first for strategic reasons rather than because it is the genuine first preference.
Assuming that meeting minimum entry requirements guarantees admission.
Using last year’s SI templates, reference forms or programme list.
Submitting vague leadership claims or unsupported work-hour calculations.
Assuming the scholarship covers insurance, family expenses, application fees or costs outside the stated award.

faq.q: Can Indian students apply for the Swedish Institute Scholarship?

runs.t: Eligibility depends on the official country list for the relevant scholarship year. Confirm that India is listed for the 2027/28 call before investing time in the application.

faq.q: Is the SI Scholarship fully funded?

runs.t: The 2027/28 call information describes tuition coverage, a monthly living allowance and a one-time travel grant. Applicants should separately budget for any excluded costs, including the University Admissions application fee, insurance and family expenses.

faq.q: How many master’s programmes can I apply for in Sweden?

runs.t: University Admissions allows up to four master’s programme choices in the first application round. The order matters because you can receive only one master’s offer.

faq.q: Can I change my ranking after 15 January 2027?

runs.t: The normal deadline to change ranking is the application deadline. Later changes may be treated as late applications and may not be considered in the ordinary selection process.

KTH requires English proficiency equivalent to Swedish upper-secondary English 6. IELTS is one accepted route, but other recognised ways of demonstrating English may apply depending on the applicant’s previous education and country-specific rules.

faq.q: Does admission to a Swedish university guarantee the SI Scholarship?

runs.t: No. University admission and SI scholarship selection are separate processes. The scholarship has its own eligibility requirements, documentation and competitive selection.
